name: NC-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with PVI of D+24
Incumbent Alma Adams running with large financial advantage
Republican challenger nearly unfunded with $3 on hand
model.rationale: Adams holds a D+24 district with a big cash advantage, while Codiga has raised under $30,000 and has essentially no money to compete. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the seat is safely Democratic.
model.watch: Only a major late scandal or redistricting-level shock would put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alma Adams, the longtime Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Charlotte-area district that leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 24 points. She has raised roughly $370,000 and holds over $450,000 in cash, giving her a comfortable financial position.

Republican Jack Codiga faces steep odds, having raised under $30,000 and reporting just $3 on hand, with no outside spending on either side. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 97 percent. The fundamentals point to a safe Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being turnout rather than the outcome itself.
